comments.note: MoviesListViewModel has two public constructors (parameterless for testing and a 7-parameter runtime constructor). Program.cs registers it with the plain AddTransient<MoviesListViewModel>() overload, relying on the DI container to select the correct constructor automatically. In .NET 10 this works because ITagsManager and all other parameters are registered. An explicit factory lambda (like the one used for MovieEditorViewModel) would remove the ambiguity and make the intended wiring self-documenting. No functional impact today.

DapperMovieCatalogRepository is registered as a singleton (AddSingleton<IMovieCatalogRepository, DapperMovieCatalogRepository>()) but its constructor accepts IDbConnectionFactory which is registered as transient. This is a captive-dependency pattern. It is safe in practice because IDbConnectionFactory is stateless and creates connections on demand, but a DI scope validator would flag it. Consider registering DapperMovieCatalogRepository with an explicit factory lambda that captures the provider and resolves IDbConnectionFactory per-call if this ever causes scope-related issues.
